ticker_news.title: Microsoft Earnings: High Capex Signals Confidence — Now the Numbers Must Deliver
ticker_news.description: Microsoft's earnings report is expected to show strong AI-driven growth in Azure Intelligent Cloud services, with commercial cloud revenue estimated at $51.2 billion (up ~25% YoY). The company's record capital spending near $100 billion signals confidence in AI demand, though investors will scrutinize whether results meet expectations. Technical analysis suggests a potential reversal of recent declines if earnings beat forecasts, with a target price around $500 per share.
ticker_news.author: Damian Nowiszewski

ticker_news.title: Only 2 "Magnificent Seven" Stocks Outperformed the S&P 500 in 2025. Are They Both Buys for 2026?
ticker_news.description: Of the Magnificent Seven tech stocks, only Nvidia (+38.9%) and Alphabet (+65.4%) outperformed the S&P 500's 16.4% return in 2025. Both are recommended as buys for long-term investors. Nvidia maintains dominance in AI chip hardware despite inevitable future competition, while Alphabet has successfully integrated AI into its search business without cannibalizing revenue.
ticker_news.author: Stefon Walters

ticker_news.title: Lantz Financial Buys $5 Million of Invesco BulletShares 2027 Corporate Bond ETF
ticker_news.description: Lantz Financial LLC purchased 270,586 shares of Invesco BulletShares 2027 Corporate Bond ETF (BSCR) for approximately $5.34 million on January 14, 2026. The investment represents 1.53% of the fund's assets under management. The purchase suggests Lantz Financial is positioning for potential interest rate declines in 2026 as inflation cools, while also increasing positions in equities like the S&P 500 ETF and Microsoft, indicating confidence in economic growth.
ticker_news.author: John Ballard

ticker_news.title: Why Less Than 10% of AI Investors Plan to Reduce Their Holdings in 2026, and 3 Stocks Worth Buying in 2026
ticker_news.description: With 90% of AI investors planning to maintain or increase holdings in 2026, the AI boom continues strong. The article recommends three stocks: Nvidia, which dominates GPU chip market with 92% share and has a $500 billion backlog; Microsoft, leveraging its enterprise relationships and OpenAI stake for AI growth; and Salesforce, trading at a 40% discount amid AI concerns but positioned to benefit from AI-enhanced products.
ticker_news.author: Justin Pope
